item.title: Draft Notice Amendment on Forest-Absorption J-Credits for Greenhouse Gas Reporting
item.description: AI summary: The proposed Notice amendment would add an entity's own efforts to preserve and enhance greenhouse gas absorption through forest management and conservation to the J-Credit scheme definition in item 4 of the domestic certified emission reductions notice. It would amend Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry and Ministry of the Environment Notice No. 3 of March 2010, supporting reporting by specified emitters under the Act on Promotion of Global Warming Countermeasures (Act No. 117 of 1998). The explanatory document states that related instruments already provide for using forest-absorption credits from an entity's own efforts to adjust its own adjusted emissions; this draft would align the credit-definition notice with those provisions. The Ministry of the Environment and Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry published the draft for public comment on 2026-11-12, with a stated deadline of 2026-12-12 00:00 JST. Issuance of the Notice is planned for January 2027, with application planned from April 1, 2027; these are proposed dates, not confirmed implementation. Original title: 「温室効果ガス算定排出量等の報告等に関する命令第一条第五号に規定する環境大臣及び経済産業大臣が定める国内認証排出削減量の一部を改正する件（案）」に対する意見募集について Public Comment Open | e-Gov Public Comment | Published 2026-11-12 | First detected 2026-11-12 Monitoring aid only; not legal advice or an official translation. item.title: Draft Notice amending greenhouse gas reporting calculations for forest-related domestic credits
item.description: AI summary: The Ministry of the Environment and the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry proposed amending their Notice No. 2 of 2025 on greenhouse gas reporting calculation methods. The draft would expand the definition of making domestic certified emission reductions non-transferable for emissions adjustment to include credits from a reporting entity's own forest management and conservation activities that preserve or enhance greenhouse gas absorption; the definition also covers other parties' emission-reduction activities. It concerns specified emitters reporting under the Act on Promotion of Global Warming Countermeasures, Act No. 117 of 1998, and Articles 4(5) and 13(3) of the greenhouse gas emissions reporting Ministerial Ordinance. The draft was published for public comment on 2026-11-12, with a stated deadline of 2026-12-12 00:00 JST. The outline schedules publication of the Notice for January 2027 and application from April 1, 2027; these are proposed dates, not confirmation of promulgation or application. item.title: FSA publishes study-group discussion summary on digital and decentralized finance
item.description: AI summary: The Financial Services Agency published a summary on 2026-11-12 of the first meeting in administrative year 2026 of its Study Group on Approaches to Digital and Decentralized Finance. Following hearings with Nomura Holdings, Inc. and Securitize Japan Co., Ltd., participants discussed on-chain finance, tokenized payment instruments and assets, and possible regulatory approaches, rather than adopted rule changes. Opinions addressed anti-money-laundering risks, financial institutions' custody and return of assets, system audit disclosures, incident controls, settlement finality and regulation of AI use. Participants also raised tokenized-deposit interoperability and questioned whether existing regulation sufficiently addresses large redemptions by major electronic payment instrument issuers and lending combined with issuance. Original title: 「デジタル・分散型金融への対応のあり方等に関する研究会」（令和８事務年度第１回）議事要旨について公表しました。 Government Announcement | Financial Services Agency (FSA) | Published 2026-11-12 | First detected 2026-11-12 Monitoring aid only; not legal advice or an official translation.
